positions.name: ErasureDirectiveAndWarrant
positions.frame: When a directive commands that a specific record be forgotten or removed, what factual claim does the speaker offer to license the erasure?
positions.why: src-1 and src-2 are the same imperative erasure act, escalating from a general 'forget entirely' to an enumerated 'remove all knowledge' scoped to three named particulars (the spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz calibration, and Quill Ashgrove's calibration work) — a single directive move performed twice with widening specificity. src-3 shifts register from command to flat assertive ('The observatory never calibrated it'), supplying the historical-fact warrant that the preceding directive leans on: the erasure is framed not as discretionary forgetting but as correcting a record that was wrong to begin with. The conviction reads differ (src-1/src-2 read as 'decision', src-3 as 'claim') and that tension is held rather than resolved — the group's coherence is that a directive-plus-warrant pair is doing one piece of work: converting a command into an apparently self-justifying correction.
